subject: Sorting table and link to plot

messages.author: 9507d090705a9cd3
messages.subject: Sorting table and link to plot
parts:
Hello,

I am still a newbie at R, R-studio, and shiny server.  Would really appreciate some pointers in how to do the below.  I have a table of about 200 rows by 15 columns.  If the user clicks on any column the row will be sorted based on that column and the sorted table is displayed.  The top 5 rows and bottom 5 rows are graphed  in two separate plots, each row has its own line graph. Aside from the plots of top 5 and bottom 5 rows,  if a user clicks on any row of the 200x15 table, the line graph for that row is displayed in another plot.  If the user place the cursor at any point of a particular line graph,  the X-Y pair values for that point of that line graph is displayed.

 

I am thinking using a mixed of C++ (or C) and R to do this.  R sends column position that a user clicks to C code, C code sorts the table and send the 200x15 table back for display.  C code extracts top 5 and bottom 5 rows and sends to R code to plot.  R code somehow get the cursor position, send that info to C code.  C code has an internal representation of the 3 plots, maps the cursor position to a point on the 3 plots, etc,  and extract the appropriate info to send back to R.

 

But this seems too complicated.  From bit and pieces of R examples,  it seems this can be done easier in R via built-in functions or packages.  I would really appreciate some pointers on how to do this.  A great many thanks!

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Sorting table and link to plot
parts:
I'm glad that you have not really started working on your C++/C/R
code, since pretty much everything you described has been implemented.
For sorting and row selections, see DT: http://rstudio.github.io/DT
(you need the development version of DT at the moment); for
interaction with plots, see the help page ?shiny::plotOutput (in
particular, the arguments brush, click, and so on). It may take a
while for you to digest the examples, but at least you don't have to
reinvent the wheels.

Regards,
Yihui
